metadata.title: Curative Title Research: How She Finds Missing Owners
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
When the owner of a property has died or disappeared, most investors walk away. Stephanie Shepherd has built her business on finding them. She's a title research specialist, California wholesaler, and joint venture partner for investors who get stuck on curative title deals.

Ten years ago, Stephanie was about to file for personal bankruptcy after a bad partnership in the surplus funds business. She started over, found a mentor, and taught herself title research through trial and error. Today investors bring her in at a forensic level: deeds from the 1800s, family trees six generations deep, name changes, adoptions, and streets that have been renamed since the original records were filed.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Stephanie and Logan Fullmer walk through exactly how she finds missing owners: why one-off skip tracing beats bulk, why she always searches the mailing address first, where data providers actually get their phone numbers, and what she says when she calls a family member so she doesn't sound like just another wholesaler.

You'll learn:
- Why one-off skip tracing gives you better data than bulk
- How to read a skip trace, and why the mailing address comes first
- Where skip tracing data really comes from
- What to say when you call a family member about a deceased owner
- How to build a family tree using Ancestry and old records
- When one house needs four probates, and when to walk away
- How she finds deals on California tax delinquent lists
- How adverse possession claims really work, and why most fail
